content:
ashton: Quick perf note — ran a 30m profiler on canary with the new batcher split. Seeing a surprising spike in 95th latency when prefill and decode share the same kernel pool. KV cache churn + kernel thrash.

sasha: ugh. do you have flame graphs?

ashton: pasted top-level here:
```
prefill: 40% idle on compute, 30% kv-sync, 20% kernel-switch, 10% memcpy
decode: 60% kernel-switch, 25% small-kernel overhead, 15% kv-wait
```

ashton: hypothesis: when prefill batches are large they hold a kernel instance that decode wants to reuse but with different sequence length -> kernel reinit and KV eviction.

liam: did this show up after the token-budget change? the 64->128 prefill bump?

ashton: yes — correlated with commit abc123 that increased prefill token goal.

nina: we already had a TODO to split phase-level queues but never wired the phase affinity. this is the nudge.

sasha: proposed quick fix: keep separate idle pools per-phase and apply kernel-affinity by model-size. cheap routing rule: if request.phase == prefill -> kernel_pool = kp_prefill_{model_shard} else kp_decode_{model_shard}.

liam: agree. Also limit prefill max_batch when decode backlog > 1. i.e. prefill.max_batch = min( configured, 16 if decode.queue_len > 1 ).

ashton: perf-bot ran a synthetic with phase isolation toggled. results: p99 reduced from 310ms -> 190ms; avg cpu utilisation + KV cache hit increased by 12%.

perf-bot: [auto] synthetic run 2025-10-12T14:02Z: p50 32ms p95 188ms p99 202ms. KV hit-rate 87%.

sasha: nice. still want to avoid hard pool explosion. maybe logical pools that map to same physical but with soft-eviction rules. e.g., mark a kernel instance as phase-favored so prefill gets preference but decode can steal with penalty.

nina: can we do that without tearing down the allocator? simplest path: implement per-phase token_budget targets + prefill backoff when decode tokens queued. config snippet: 
```yaml
runtime:
  queues:
    prefill:
      token_budget_target: "72"
      max_batch: "24"
      backoff_if_decode_queue_gt: "1"
    decode:
      token_budget_target: "8"
      max_batch: "8"
```
backoff rule: reduce prefill token_budget_target by 50% when decode.queue_len > backoff_if_decode_queue_gt

liam: That should be low risk. Would like a guard: only enable backoff for models with seq_len < 2048 to avoid hurting long-context prefill.

ashton: also flagged a regression: on the canary run one model saw 6% token throughput drop during peak even though latency improved overall. suspect kernel selection path still favors smaller kernels for larger dynamic seq_len.

sasha: can you attach a single-request trace? need kernel selection decision tree with inputs (seq_len, batch_size, quant_mode).

ashton: attached in the thread (gist): https://gist.github.com/redwood/ashton-prefill-kerneltrace

deploy-bot: [deploy] rolled prefill/decode-queue-split v0.3.2 to canary at 2259999060

nina: action items: 1) add per-phase logical pools + soft affinity (sasha) 2) token-budget backoff rule + seq_len guard (liam) 3) validate kernel selector heuristics for large seq len (ashton) 4) long-run perf job (perf-bot)

sasha: ETA for logical pools: start PR today, ready for review EOD.

liam: PR for backoff rule and config validation by tomorrow AM.

ashton: i'll benchmark kernel selector changes and post updated flame graphs.

perf-bot: [scheduled] 6h load test queued: job id rt-2259-01

nina: thanks all — goal: merge canary changes if 24h load test keeps p99 < 220ms and no throughput regression > 2%.

sasha: cool. will add a brief doc note about the phase affinity heuristics for oncall.

liam: ping me if you want me to run bisect on the kernel commits. i can do a binary search on kernel tweaks.

ashton: will do.

sasha: closing loop — pretty confident split + backoff will avoid KV thrash while keeping batching efficiency high. :thumbsup:
